nodes.label: UAE-account Stripe customer for credit purchases
Rationale: credits always bill on UAE, so a legacy-account tenant needs a second Stripe customer that must never overwrite stripe_subscription_customer_id
New tenants default to UAE billing account and own-Stripe OAuth model
Rationale: changing only the DEFAULT is a segment-1-only move — existing trading tenants keep their values and are migrated deliberately, one at a time
Close the unauthenticated read of tenant secrets on public.tenants
Rationale: Twilio suspension root cause — RLS off plus a table-level anon SELECT let any visitor read plaintext twilio_auth_token / bonzah_password via PostgREST
Rationale: a column-level REVOKE is a no-op while the table-level SELECT stands (Postgres authorizes a column read by table-grant OR column-grant)
Anon column allow-list on tenants — explicit non-secret columns only
Anon loses every write privilege on tenants and the allow_all insert/delete policies are dropped
Secrecy by column grant, not by row filter — tenants_public_select stays USING(true) so no booking site regresses
Known residual gap: authenticated still holds table-level SELECT because five select('*') sites in portal/admin would break — deferred to Phase 2
Go-live stamping for operators — setup_completed_at backfill plus a BEFORE UPDATE trigger
Rationale: live operators were mislabeled 'Setup Mode' because setup_completed_at was only ever stamped on the trial→active webhook path
Went-live predicate: stripe_mode='live' AND stripe_account_status='active' (not the managed-only stripe_onboarding_complete flag)
Rationale: backfilled timestamp capped to >2 days ago so the 24h "You're Live!" banner does not fire retroactively for 17 tenants
Per-category idempotency guard when generating a rental's first charges
Rationale: the portal's pre-inserted Bonzah Insurance charge tripped a coarse whole-function guard, so Rental/Tax/Service Fee were never created and a $131.33 payment bound only $50.13
Invoice-to-ledger category split (Rental, Tax, Service Fee, Insurance, Delivery Fee, Collection Fee, Extras) with a single-charge fallback when no invoice exists
Accept the complete Stripe subscription status set, including incomplete_expired
Rationale: one rejected status makes the handler throw, Stripe retries ~3 days and can AUTO-DISABLE the endpoint, killing delivery of every other subscription event
Rationale: Stripe API 2025-03-31 (basil) moved current_period_start/end onto subscription ITEMS, so unguarded writes produced new Date(NaN) → RangeError → HTTP 500 on every subscription.updated
Sync-provenance metadata on tenant_subscriptions (last_stripe_event_at, last_synced_at, last_sync_source)
Out-of-order protection: an older Stripe event must never overwrite newer state, and the reconciler must not clobber fresher webhook data
Dunning fields for the grace clock (next_payment_attempt, attempt_count, billing_reason)
Rationale: due_date is NULL on all 51 invoice rows (everything is charge_automatically), so the grace clock derives from current_period_end / next_payment_attempt instead
Hourly pg_cron schedule for the subscription reconciler
Rationale: webhooks are a DELIVERY guarantee, not a CONSISTENCY guarantee — a 7-day handler crash left 9 tenants marked canceled who were actually active
Cadence trade-off: hourly at minute 17 bounds worst-case drift to an hour while staying inside Stripe rate limits and off other jobs' tick
Secret hygiene: the job command is cloned from an existing cron job so the service_role key is never written into a migration in source control
Per-tenant Google tag (GA4 measurement ID) for the booking site
Rationale: after the anon allow-list lockdown, any NEW tenants column is unreadable to anon until explicitly granted — without the grant the tag would silently never load
Existing gtag('event', …) calls in the booking flow are no-ops until a tenant supplies the base script id
Portal feedback channel — staff report bugs about the Drive247 software to super admins
Naming boundary: tenant_feedback_* is NOT rental_reviews (staff rating customers) nor feedback_submissions (renter testimonials)
Attribution snapshot: app_user_id is nullable ON DELETE SET NULL with submitter_name/email/role denormalised so a departing staff member cannot delete their own bug reports
notified_at stamp makes the feedback alert mailer idempotent against retries, double-clicks and replayed requests
Own-rows-only read policy — deliberately not tenant-wide, because a viewer has no business reading the head admin's complaint about the software
Insert policy pins identity and state: file as yourself, for your own tenant, status='open' with resolved_at/resolved_by NULL
The ABSENT INSERT policy on tenant_feedback_insights is the control that stops a browser forging an 'AI summary'
feedback-screenshots is a PRIVATE bucket because a portal screenshot routinely contains customer PII (names, addresses, licence images, card last4)
Structurally enforced singleton settings row (UNIQUE CHECKed boolean) so a second config the app never reads cannot exist
Case-insensitive recipient uniqueness so Ops@ and ops@ cannot double-mail the same person
app_users.feedback_last_prompted_at drives both prompt throttles: the 7-day rental-completion cooldown and the force-show-on-next-login comparison
Narrow screenshot reads to the submitter's own rows, matching the row policy exactly
Rationale: the tenant-wide storage grant let any staff member list and sign every screenshot in their tenant folder — including a Payments screen a manager is denied by permissions
source column records which entry point produced a submission (sidebar / rental_close / forced)
Rationale: source was previously smuggled into page_path ("/rentals/abc (forced-login)"), corrupting the only reproduction field the schema captures
SECURITY DEFINER stamp so the portal never needs a direct UPDATE grant on app_users
Rationale: the self-UPDATE policy authorising the browser write (p_update_own_password_flag) carries no column list, so it also let any portal user set their own is_super_admin
Platform Terms of Service acceptance recorded against the OPERATOR (tenant), with evidentiary who/when/email/IP
Rationale: terms_version / policies_accepted_at / policy_acceptances are a DIFFERENT system (tenant's own policy, accepted by staff) and settings resets policies_accepted_at on every version edit

Deliberately no anon grant: these columns must never enter TENANT_CORE_COLUMNS, because Postgres refuses the WHOLE ROW when one selected column is ungranted — that already took down login once (customer_theme_mode)
Accepted ToS version is derived SERVER-side from _shared/platform-tos.ts, never taken from the request body; write-once and service_role only
Stamp tenant_id on every vehicle-lifecycle P&L writer and backfill the existing orphans
Rationale: a tenant_id-NULL P&L row falls outside the operator's RLS scope, so the portal's cleanup delete matches nothing and the vehicle delete then fails on the FK
payment_apply_fifo_v2 already stamped tenant_id on payment-driven P&L rows; this extends the same backfill to acquisition, disposal, service, plate and fine entries
Vehicle deletion unblocked: pnl_entries and reminder_events cascade in the database, beneath RLS, atomically with the vehicle
Rationale: the portal's four unchecked non-transactional child deletes destroyed some children, then failed the vehicle delete on the FK — and re-adding the vehicle then failed on vehicles_reg_key
Decision: owner_payout_lines stays ON DELETE RESTRICT — erasing payout history to make a delete convenient is the wrong trade; the operator is pointed at Dispose instead
tenantAlreadyLive guard suppressing the portal Setup Mode chip
reconcile-subscriptions edge function (repairs Stripe drift across all four account x mode cells)
